The contract should include the following warranty requirements:

* Products and services are guaranteed to be free from defects in design, materials, workmanship, manufacture or programming.

##### Additional topics to consider for this topic

In addition to the following clauses, it is good practice:

* to allow for 12 months of warranty to allow enough time for defects to occur during usage (and this is also best industry practice).
* not to rely on clauses that simply say, for the "Warranty, indemnities and limit of liability provisions, see Annexure A.".
* add warranty provisions that clarify whether it also includes liability and indemnities for any products that are supplied with the warranty-product. For example, if a "kit" is warranted (for 12 months) but is made up of two sub-components, and one of the sub-components only lasts 6 months - which element of the contract contains the warranty, and which contains the limited liability element?
* do not forget the limitations of liability of the supplier (the one responsible for the faulty parts!)

A given match label (label, not clause) can be associated with any of two or more clauses, depending on how that clause is used in the contract population. This can cause us to calculate the match ratio a given label over any of several clauses which we label "instances" of the label in question: an instance represents the association of a match label to a different but identical clause each time it appears in the sample population, with some clauses possibly appearing several times with different label/instance combinations for each different instance of its associated label.
